entities.summary: Eleanor Jack Gibson was an American psychologist who focused on reading development and perceptual learning in infants. Gibson began her career at Smith College as an instructor in 1932, publishing her first works on research conducted as an undergraduate student. Gibson was able to circumvent the many obstacles she faced due to the Great Depression and gender discrimination, by finding research opportunities that she could meld with her own interests. Gibson, with her husband James J. Gibson, created the Gibsonian ecological theory of development, which emphasized how important perception was because it allows humans to adapt to their environments.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Eleanor Gibson's work on perceptual learning in infants and her development of the Gibsonian ecological theory had a significant impact on our understanding of infant development and cognition. Her research laid the foundation for future studies in developmental psychology.
